bloc.Activation et suivi — accès complet à la: Activation and follow-up — full access to the Sentinel platform, continuous measurement of your progress, and billing of each milestone only after the result achieved has been verified

bloc.Ce que cela implique. C’est la réponse l: What this implies. It is the most frequent answer, and it can be dealt with: put the product through the Simulator before deciding the other five points, because the answer changes what they must contain.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. C’est le vecteur d: What this implies. It is the most direct attack vector opened by assisted development, and it requires no access to your information system from the attacker.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Dans six mois, plu: What this implies. In six months, nobody will know which files were produced this way. The day a systematic defect is discovered in a family of generations, you will not be able to know where to look.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Décision légitime,: What this implies. A legitimate decision, provided it is enforced. Prohibiting without any means of detecting it produces clandestine use: the generated code gets in anyway, and without any of the checks of point #.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Déplace la charge: What this implies. Shifts the burden onto the review, which becomes the real checkpoint. Choose it only if the reviewers have the time and the mandate to refuse.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Il faut alors que: What this implies. “Security code” must then be defined somewhere, file by file or module by module. A boundary that everyone interprets is not a boundary: it moves at the first tight deadline.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. La documentation t: What this implies. The technical documentation must then describe the development process, including methods and tools (art. # and Annex IV). An unwritten assisted-development policy becomes a missing document in the file, detectable during the conformity assessment.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. La restriction la: What this implies. The easiest restriction to maintain, and the one that pays off least. Beware of false comfort: a generated test that tests nothing lets through what it was meant to catch, and nobody notices as long as nothing breaks.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. La règle la plus s: What this implies. The simplest and clearest rule. It assumes that producing assisted code carries the same commitment as writing it — so that review time is counted as working time, not taken out of the announced gain.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. La seule réponse s: What this implies. The only safe answer. Models invent plausible package names, and attackers publish those invented names waiting for someone to install them — installing is enough to run their code.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Le code de sûreté: What this implies. Safety and security code then goes through the same path as the rest. It is tenable if — and only if — the reinforced review of point # applies to it in full, which requires reviewers who know it.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Le plus durable, l: What this implies. The most durable, the noisiest. Reserve it for areas where the origin changes what a reviewer must do — otherwise the marking becomes noise that people stop reading.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Le réglage courant: What this implies. The usual setting, and the one that requires the most discipline: a secret pasted into a prompt is a disclosed secret, and the only remedy is to rotate it. Plan the rotation procedure before you need it, not after.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Le service ne voit: What this implies. The service never sees your code. It is the only setting where the question of confidentiality does not arise, and it greatly reduces the help obtained.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Les cinq décisions: What this implies. The five decisions above remain internal engineering decisions. Still check that the answer will be true in a year: a product changes qualification by changing its use, not by changing its code.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Plus strict encore: What this implies. Stricter still, at the cost of real friction on new projects. Consistent with a reproducible build chain.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. Traçable et peu co: What this implies. Traceable and inexpensive. The link is lost at the first history rewrite or the first file port, but it holds in ordinary use.
bloc.Ce que cela implique. À n’envisager que: What this implies. Consider only under a contract that explicitly excludes reuse for training, with a known processing location. If personal data are involved, sending them is a transfer within the meaning of the GDPR, with everything that entails.
bloc.Ce que nous faisons à la place, quand la: What we do instead, when the question arises: we write with you what the position must deliver — the scope, the decisions it carries, what it will have to be able to demonstrate — and you entrust the recruitment to a specialist firm, which we can help brief. We say so before the commercial proposal, not after signature: a skill we do not have, and that we let people hope for, costs the client more than a refusal.

bloc.Non pas « une relecture » : une signatur: Not “a re-read”: a signature — someone named who answers for the decision, and who can be questioned about it in two years’ time. “The AI wrote it” has never been an admissible answer, whether before an auditor, a judge or the on-call team.
bloc.Pourquoi ce point n’existe pas sur du co: Why this point does not exist for written code. It is the only point that cannot be caught up later. Code whose reasons nobody knows cannot be maintained: at the first change, it gets rewritten, and the announced gain is paid back with interest.

Why this point does not exist for written code. The trap specific to generated code: a test written from the implementation always passes, including when the implementation is wrong. The test must come from what is EXPECTED, not from what was produced.

Why this point does not exist for written code. Generations readily add a neighbouring feature, an option, a cache. What was not asked for was not specified, so not reviewed, so not tested — and yet it ends up in production.

Why this point does not exist for written code. A generated comment is just as assertive when it is wrong. A reviewer who relies on it reads the same error twice: in the intention and in the code, without ever comparing them.

Why this point does not exist for written code. A memorised excerpt arrives without its header. On thirty or so lines of code that resemble a known project, the question arises — and it arises before publication, not after.

Why this point does not exist for written code. A model first produces what works. A person writing code runs into the edge cases along the way; a generation goes around them without ever meeting them, and the code looks complete.

Why this point does not exist for written code. A model produces a plausible package name with the same confidence as a real one. Attackers publish these invented names relying precisely on this regularity. A human reviewer never spontaneously checks that an import exists: they assume the author knew.
bloc.Tout code qui décide d’un droit d’une pe: Any code that decides on a person’s rightRefusal, price, score, referral, penalty. The person concerned has the right to know who answers for it.
bloc.Une transformation IA-first fait presque: An AI-first transformation almost always raises the question of recruitment: which profiles, what level, how to assess them. That is not our business. CONSEILPREV does not source developers, does not assess technical level and does not conduct job interviews. We have neither the talent pool, nor the assessment method, nor the legal responsibility that goes with it.
